steps.title: Preserve the current VF2 evidence and provide space for a fresh matrix
verification: Before the first media mutation, tell the user the exact source, target node, serial, capacity, operation, validation, and rollback evidence
Re-identify the removable USB device by serial 121220160204, 31719424000-byte capacity, USB transport, removable=1, whole-device ext4 layout, not mounted, and not the host root device
Set the block device read-only and create a complete verified backup of the current card before any resize or overwrite
Rehearse whole-device ext4 resize on a working copy, then verify the retained VF2 acceptance directory, hashes, commits, and e2fsck -fn before requesting final physical-media authorization
After authorized resize, return the block device to read-only, require e2fsck -fn exit 0, verify old evidence read-only, and power off the reader
steps.notes: This gate does not block merge or QEMU. The card currently has about 6 MiB free. Preferred remediation is verified full-card backup plus rehearsed whole-device resize; rewriting the Alpine baseline is disaster recovery only because it erases current evidence. No first write occurs silently.

steps.title: Reproduce the full VF2 RW-reset-RO matrix with the merge artifact
verification: Boot the uniquely named merge uImage after host SHA/mkimage checks and U-Boot iminfo, using transient variables and tx.root=mmcblk0 rw
Confirm /dev/mmcblk0 whole-device ext4 RW, valid UTC/CA/network/default route/DNS, ps -ef, Git help/init/commit/log/fsck, a real full-screen Vim edit, and GCC/Rust Hello World compile and execution
Create a new full non-shallow clone directory, verify remote/original HEAD, object count, shallow=false, local evidence commit, clean status, and git fsck --full
Record manifests and hashes, call sync twice, stop userspace cleanly, request one physical reset, then boot the same uImage and same MMC with tx.root=mmcblk0 ro
On RO boot, recheck ext4 RO, all file hashes and binaries, both Git repositories and commits, non-shallow state, clean status, and git fsck --full
If credentialed push reproduction is required, the user performs it and supplies an attestation; the agent does not read, search, copy, or retain PAT-bearing output
steps.notes: The capacity gate in step 8 is mandatory. Do not delete the previous acceptance evidence. Pull is not a prior verified requirement and remains outside the gate unless the user explicitly adds it. A sync return is not durability proof; only the physical reset plus independent RO readback closes this step.

steps.title: Reproduce the LA2K1000 RO-RW-reset-RO persistence matrix
verification: Copy the freshly rebuilt kernel-only uImage to a unique TFTP name with cp --no-clobber, then require cmp, direct sha256sum on both files, and U-Boot iminfo CRC success

Intercept U-Boot, run scsi reset, verify the expected disk model and 62533296 by 512 geometry, and stop if the observed root layout differs from the current sda1 tutorial or the older raw-ext4 sda handoff
First boot read-only with the observed root token, tx.mount.sdcard=0, and no initrd; require AHCI, DWMAC, ext4 root, boot:ok, and an explicit RO mount

After RO and network gates pass, physically reset and boot RW with tx.ext4.rw-profile=legacy-nocsum, then run the fresh add-only Git/tool persistence workload with individual short commands and explicit fsync/syncfs/sync completion
Physically reset again, boot the same disk RO, and verify commits, hashes, executions, non-shallow state where exercised, and git fsck --full --no-progress
steps.notes: LA2K1000 loads only the kernel uImage by TFTP and reuses the existing SATA ext4 root. Do not dd, mkfs, repartition, mmc write, sf write, saveenv, run repair fsck, or trust target/images/txv2-la2k1000.uimage.sha256. If the disk appears as raw-ext4 sda rather than sda1, stop and reconcile the active handoff before booting RW.

verification.command: Fresh host/QEMU/VF2/LA2K1000 validation from the merge commit
verification.notes: The user approved merge execution and directed QEMU to run first. VF2 capacity remediation and both physical-board reset checkpoints remain later interactive gates.

risks: A clean textual merge can still violate the PageBacked lifetime or Process fd/signal state machines; focused semantic audit and tests are mandatory.
Old QEMU result JSON and VF2 uImage hashes identify pre-merge kernels and cannot attest the merge commit.
Shared init/reactor changes from VF2 can regress QEMU boot even where there is no textual conflict.
The VF2 MMC barrier can report success without a physical flush, so sync alone is not an acceptance criterion.
Global gates are already red for documented unrelated reasons; comparison must distinguish an unchanged baseline from a new merge regression.
A stale LA2K1000 checksum sidecar can falsely identify a rebuilt image unless the artifact itself is hashed.
blockers: The retained VF2 MMC acceptance filesystem has about 6 MiB free, below the space needed for a fresh add-only full clone and persistence matrix. This blocks only the later VF2 physical phase; it does not block merge or QEMU. Before the first media mutation, the exact target and evidence-preserving backup/resize procedure must be explained to the user.
